invariants.text: Product.product_id must be an auto-incremented integer primary key with default value None

If the bulk update operation is invoked, all products specified in the update must have their stock quantity modified atomically; if any product fails to update, the entire transaction must roll back and no changes must be applied to any product.
The stock quantity of a product must not be reduced below zero during any operation, including bulk updates.
A product's stock quantity after a bulk update must reflect the new value provided in the update request, and must not be modified by any other operation until the transaction is committed.

The bulk update operation must only accept a list of product IDs and a new stock quantity value, and must not allow different stock quantity values for different products unless explicitly supported by a separate bulk update mechanism.
Any change to a product's stock quantity via CRUD operations must be consistent with the state of the database at the time of the operation, and must not allow partial updates.
If a product does not exist in the inventory when attempting to update its stock quantity, the bulk update operation must fail and not apply any changes to any other product.

The bulk update operation must ensure that all products in the update list are updated with the same new stock quantity value, unless the operation is designed to handle per-product updates with explicit support.
The stock quantity of a product after a successful update must be equal to the value specified in the update request, and must not be derived from any other product's value.
All CRUD operations on products must maintain data integrity, ensuring that no product is created with a negative stock quantity.
The bulk update operation must be executed within a transaction that ensures all changes are either fully committed or fully rolled back, with no partial updates applied to the database.
